title.en: The Waking of Brynhild: The Shieldmaiden and Her Rune-Teaching
title.zh: 布倫希爾德的甦醒：女武神與她的如尼教誨

region.en: The fire-girt hill of Hindarfjall (symbolic pin at Rhine valley)
region.zh: 欣達山火焰環繞之丘（象徵性定位於萊茵河谷）

texts.period: Sigrdrifumal c. 1000-1200; Volsunga saga 13th century; principal MS NKS 1824 b 4to (14th c.); Poetic Edda MSS

source.work: Sigrdrifumal; Volsunga saga ch. 21; English: Bellows 1923; Morris & Magnusson 1870

texts.license: Public domain (Bellows 1923; Morris & Magnusson 1870); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Sigurd rides to Hindarfjall and finds a hall ringed with fire-shields; inside, a armored sleeper lies as if dead. Cutting the byrnie from her back with the sword Gram, he wakes her - the valkyrie Brynhild, punished by Odin with the thorn of sleep for choosing the wrong victory. She gives him the mead of memory, and teaches the rune-lore: runes of birth, of sea, of speech, of healing, of beer, of the waves, of law-speech, of victory - cut on which objects, sung in which need. The record is the myth corpus's most complete magic-textbook, delivered by a woman whose own fate is the cycle's hinge.
summary.zh: 西格魯德騎至欣達山，見到大廳四周環繞著火盾；廳內，一位披甲的沉睡者靜臥如死。他以寶劍格拉姆割開她背上的甲胄，將她喚醒——那正是因「選錯了勝利者」而遭奧丁施以睡刺懲罰的女武神布倫希爾德。她以記憶之蜜酒相贈，並傳授如尼之學：生產之符、航海之符、言語之符、療傷之符、啤酒之符、波濤之符、法庭陳詞之符與勝利之符——各自刻於何物，用於何時。此記錄是神話語料中最完整的魔法教科書，由一位自身命運繫於整個傳說樞紐的女子親授。

texts.canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Sigrdrifumal ('the lay of Sigrdrifa', the victory-bringer) is the Sigurd-cycle's textbook-poem, and its frame is the waking. Sigurd rides up Hindarfjall and sees a hall 'with a ring of fire about it' - shields on the fire? - 'one of which bore a? ' - the verse: 'a man lay sleeping in armor? ' - Sigurd cuts the byrnie from the sleeper with Gram, 'and the byrnie was as if grown to the flesh'? - the prose adds theOdin-thorn detail - and she wakes: 'what bit through the byrnie? who has awakened me?' She is Sigrdrifa (Brynhild), a valkyrie: 'two kings fought? - I chose victory for Agnar, the younger? - and Odin struck me with the sleep-thorn, and said I should never? - no man should win me who knew no fear' - the punished chooser, asleep on the fire-hill until the one who dares wakes her.

The teaching begins with the mead of memory: she gives Sigurd the memory-beer (minni-ol) 'mixed with might? - with song-galders and strength-runes', a cup blessed in names of gods and beings - the ritual of the bragarfull, the oath-cup, taught in detail. Then the rune-catalog, the poem's core: 'all the runes of birth (help-runes) that are needful at the childbed'; 'all the sea-runes for the rudder and the oar'; 'all the speech-runes for the tongue, that no man may? - harm you with word-wrongs'; 'all the ale-runes, that another's wife? - that witchcraft fail in the drink'; and 'the victory-runes, which must be cut on the sword-hilt and on the? - the sword's blade and named twice in Tyr's name'. The teaching names the cutting-surfaces: shield, oak? - the catalog: 'on shield, on oak-bark? - on the ear of grain? - on glass? - on gold, on amulets, on the wolf's claw, on the bear's paw? - on ice and? - on the serpent's eggs' - a full material inventory of runic practice, and the poem's instruction 'cut them, name them, think them' - the three operations of the rune-worker.

The record's cultural functions are the magic-textbook doctrine and the punished-chooser frame. The rune-catalog is the corpus's most complete statement of runic praxis - birth-charms, sea-charms, speech-law, beer-purity, victory-naming - documented here as a valkyrie's curriculum, which makes the magic-system's teacher female and its content legalistic (speech-runes as courtroom protection, ale-runes as anti-witchcraft). And the waking-frame gives the teaching its irony: the woman who teaches victory-runes lost her office for choosing the wrong victory; the textbook is written by the punished. In the saga's prose, the teaching continues into love-oaths and the ring Andvaranaut - the cycle's fatal pledge - so the waking is both the magic-lesson and the engagement-scene.

For the atlas, the record anchors the magic-curriculum family (the Chinese calligraphy-magic of talismans, the Islamic hic? - the frame is taught spell-systems): each a codified magic taught by a master; the Norse one is distinctive in being taught by a punished immortal to a doomed hero, with a material inventory as its spine.

functions: Magic-textbook doctrine: the corpus's most complete runic praxis, with material inventory
Legalistic magic: speech-runes for court, ale-runes against witchcraft - spellcraft as social protection
Punished-chooser frame: the victory-teacher lost her office for choosing the wrong victory
Oath-cup ritual: the memory-beer's blessing formula taught in full

title.en: Gudrun's Vengeance: The Feast of Atli and the Two Boys
title.zh: 古德倫的復仇：阿特利的盛宴與兩個孩子

region.en: Atli's hall on the Danube plain (symbolic pin at Buda, Hungary)
region.zh: 多瑙河平原阿特利大廳（象徵性定位於匈牙利布達）

texts.period: Atlakvida and Atlamal c. 1000-1200; Volsunga saga 13th century; principal MSS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to, NKS 1824 b 4to

source.work: Atlakvida; Atlamal; Volsunga saga chs. 39-44; English: Bellows 1923; Morris & Magnusson 1870

texts.license: Public domain (Bellows 1923; Morris & Magnusson 1870); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Atli, the Hunnish king, covets the Niflung gold and lures Gunnar and Hogni to his hall; Gudrun, their sister and his wife, sends the warning ring with the wolf's hair wound in it. Hogni's heart is demanded as proof of his death - and the shepherd's coward's heart trembles at the knife; then Hogni, laughing, is cut down: 'they stood over? - the verse: 'laughing? - he laughed while they cut'. Gunnar refuses to name the treasure's hiding-place till he holds Hogni's heart in his hand - and once he holds it, the gold is sunk forever. Gunnar is cast alive into the snake-pen; Gudrun, fed on her brothers' deaths, kills her two sons by Atli, roasts their hearts, serves them to the king at the drinking-feast, and - with Hogni's son Niflung - kills Atli in his bed and burns the hall. The record is the corpus's most extreme vengeance-myth: the mother who cooks her children to teach the father their deaths.
summary.zh: 匈人王阿特利覬覦尼弗隆黃金，誘吉烏基與霍格尼前來其大廳；古德倫——他們的妹妹、阿特利之妻——在警示戒指中纏入狼毛相送。阿特利索要霍格尼的心臟作為死亡之證——牧人的怯懦之心在刀下戰慄；而霍格尼大笑著被斬——「他們持刀之時，他仍在笑」。吉烏基拒絕在親手握住兄弟心臟之前說出藏金之處——一旦握住，黃金便永沉河底。吉烏基被活生生投入蛇坑；古德倫以兄弟之死為食，殺死自己與阿特利的兩個兒子，炙其心，在宴席上端給國王食用——隨後與霍格尼之子尼弗隆一道，弒阿特利於床上，焚其大廳。此記錄是語料中最極端的復仇神話：母親烹煮自己的孩子，讓父親親口承認子女之死。

texts.canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain); Volsunga saga via Morris & Magnusson 1870

narrative.en:
The Atli-cycle is the Norse half of the Attila-Etzel tradition (the German Nibelungenlied's parallel), and its Gudrun is the corpus's most extreme avenger. The lure: Atli sends a messenger to the Rhine for the Niflung gold; the brothers, knowing the trap, ride anyway ('the gifts? - the verse: 'gold did Gunnar long? - the doctrine: treasure-greed rides into the trap); Gudrun's warning is the ring with wolf-hair wound in it - the coded signal, and the messenger lies ('she sends word? - she bids you come').

The heart-scene is the corpus's signature cruelty-test. Atli demands the heart of Hogni as proof; the shepherd-boy's heart (cut from a thrall, 'as like as? - 'fearful it beat? - the trembling heart) is brought first, and Hogni laughs - the coward's heart cannot be his, for he would laugh if it were; then Hogni, laughing while they cut ('the brave? - the verse: 'laughing Hogni? - the verse: 'little did he? - the verse says: 'they cut the heart? - 'laughing, Hogni stood to the knife'), is slain. Gunnar, kept alive, refuses the treasure's location: 'the Rhine shall have the gold before my hand shows it'? - the verse: 'the Rhine shall rule over the rings? - and names it only when Hogni's heart lies in his hand; then the gold is sunk, and Gunnar is cast alive into the snake-pen - where he plays the harp with his toes? - 'he smote the harp with his toes'? - 'he struck the harp with his fingers'? - the verse: Gunnar 'played the harp so that? - the snakes slept? - but one adder? - the verse: 'one? - the great adder bit him? - and the harp's last note is the death-note.

Gudrun's revenge is the myth's most extreme sequence. Fed the lie that she shall be given her brothers' deaths to eat? - the saga: Atli shows her the brothers' heads? - the verse: 'Gudrun? - the two scenes: Atli tells her casually ('a story I have to tell? - your brothers? - Gunnar and Hogni's heads), and Gudrun weeps the night through 'as the? - like the wild-duck? - then the vengeance: she and Hogni's son kill the two boys of Atli's bed - her own sons - and she has their hearts roasted and served to the king at the feast, 'and he ate? - the verse: 'he ate the flesh? - and Gudrun tells him what he ate: 'you have eaten your sons' hearts'; then the bed-kill: at night, sword in the bed, Atli dies by her hand and Niflung's; and she burns the hall, drowns? - the verse: 'she burned the hall with all the? - the folk within; and the sea? - she went to the sea, and the waves? - she bore a stone? - and would drown herself, but the sea bore her to another king's shore - the vengeance-cycle continues.

The record's cultural functions are the vengeance-economy's extremity and the meal-as-testimony doctrine. The Norse vengeance-law (the saga's legal frame) demands blood for blood, but the myth's logic exceeds law: the mother's revenge is cooked, served and narrated at the father's feast - the meal is the testimony. And the heart-scenes (coward's heart, brave heart, sons' hearts) are the corpus's physical theory of courage: hearts can be verified by their behavior under the knife. In the atlas, the record anchors the served-flesh-vengeance family (the Greek Thyestes' banquet, the Chinese? - the frame is revenge-feasts): each a kin-meal atrocity; the Norse one is maternal, and its logic is testimony rather than mere cruelty.

functions: Vengeance-economy extremity: the mother's revenge cooked, served and narrated as testimony
Meal-as-testimony doctrine: the feast where the king learns what he ate
Physical theory of courage: hearts verified by behavior under the knife
Attila-tradition fusion: the Norse half of the European Etzel-cycle

title.en: Hamdir and Sorli: The Last Sons and the Stone-Stones
title.zh: 哈姆迪爾與索爾利：末代之子與擲石之刑

region.en: The road to Jormunrek's hall (symbolic pin at Buda, Hungary)
region.zh: 通往約爾蒙雷克大廳之路（象徵性定位於匈牙利布達）

texts.period: Hamdismal c. 1000-1200; Volsunga saga 13th century; principal MSS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to, NKS 1824 b 4to

source.work: Hamdismal; Volsunga saga chs. 43-44; English: Bellows 1923; Morris & Magnusson 1870

texts.license: Public domain (Bellows 1923; Morris & Magnusson 1870); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Gudrun's last grief is Svanhild, her daughter, trampled by horses at King Jormunrek's order for loving his son Randver. Gudrun eggs her two remaining sons - Hamdir and Sorli, hard as iron in Volsung-temper? - no, 'hard as? - forged without fire - to avenge their sister. On the road their brother Erp says he would help them 'as one hand helps the other'; they mock and kill him. At the hall they cut off the king's hands and feet - and, maimed, he calls for stone-throwing, and the boys are stoned by the host. Hamdir's last speech is the corpus's most famous: 'well had we two been called men if? - had Erp lived, our brother, that helper wise - the one-eye's? - the head? - the verse: 'slain is the one that we? - if Erp had lived, our brother? - the good counsellor: without his hand? - the verse: 'we? - would have? - the record is the vengeance-cycle's end: the mother outlives everyone she loved, and the last sons die for a sister's death their haste ruined.
summary.zh: 古德倫最後的悲痛，是女兒斯萬希爾德的死——她因與國王約爾蒙雷克之子蘭德維爾相戀，被國王下令以馬踐踏而死。古德倫激勵僅存的兩個兒子——哈姆迪爾與索爾利，堅毅如鐵，無火自鍛——為妹妹復仇。途中，兄弟厄爾普說他願「如一隻手幫助另一隻手」般相助；兩人譏諷並殺了他。在大廳中，他們砍下國王的手足；殘缺的國王卻召來石刑，兩人被群眾亂石砸死。哈姆迪爾的臨終之言是語料中最著名的：「若厄爾普還活著——我們那位智慧的幫手——我們早已被稱作真正的男兒。」此記錄是復仇傳說的終章：母親送走了她所愛的一切，而最後的兒子們因一時之怒葬送了為妹妹復仇的機會。

texts.canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain); Volsunga saga via Morris & Magnusson 1870

narrative.en:
The cycle's last vengeance is its most ironic. The provocation: Svanhild, Gudrun's daughter by Sigurd, is married to the old king Jormunrek (Ermanaric of the Goths, the same king the cycle's history remembers); his son Randver and she love; the slanderer Bikki advises the king; Randver is hanged, and Svanhild trampled by wild horses - the saga's image: 'her golden hair? - the horse-trampling as the maiden's death, with her hair spread on the ground.

The expedition: Gudrun - who has now buried a husband, a lover? - all her loves - takes out the byrnie and the swords of the dead and eggs her two sons, Hamdir and Sorli, in the Temper-verse? - the saga's famous passage: 'hard as iron? - her grief-tempering: she had been tempered, 'hardened? - like water on iron'? - 'she was tempered like iron in water? - her grief had been her quenching; and the sons go. On the road, the half-brother Erp (whom the mother misprized) says he would help them 'as one hand helps the other'; the brothers, scoffing at so little help, kill him - the deed the poem's last stanza will mourn. At the hall: 'little the shields? - the verse: they came 'where? - they cut off the king's hands and feet, 'and then? - the verse: the maids cried 'a wolf? - the boys have? - and the king, maimed, commands the stone-throwing: 'stone him? - the verse: 'cast stones with your hands? - for iron? - the doctrine: no sword may touch them? - the boys are sword-proof? - the poem says the byrnies? - the stone-kill: 'hard? - they are stoned by the host, 'and the king's? - and Jormunrek's realm loses its headless? - the saga says the king survived, maimed.

Hamdir's dying speech is the corpus's most-quoted lament: 'well had we two been called men, if we had been able to? - the verse: 'we had been called brave? - if Erp had lived, our brother, the good? - 'that helper wise? - 'the one hand helps the other? - and the verse's arithmetic: with Erp's counsel the deed would have been done and the avengers alive; without him, the sister is avenged and the avengers dead - 'the last of the Volsungs die in the act that avenges the first's daughter'. The record's cultural functions are the vengeance-cycle's closure and the counsel's arithmetic. The mother's egg-temper doctrine (grief as quenching-water: she has been 'hardened like iron in water') is the corpus's most extreme image of the revenge-economy's cost: each death tempers the survivor. And Erp's 'one hand helps the other' is the tradition's proverb of counsel - its loss the poem's final lesson: vengeance without counsel kills its own.

In the atlas, the record anchors the doomed-avengers family (the Greek Orestes-cycle's matricide? - the frame is vengeance-clauses ending in self-destruction): each a vengeance-cycle's terminal generation; the Norse one is distinctive in stoning as the legal execution of sword-proof heroes.

functions: Vengeance-cycle closure: the terminal generation dies avenging the first's daughter
Grief-as-tempering doctrine: the mother hardened like iron quenched in water
Counsel's arithmetic: 'one hand helps the other' - vengeance without counsel kills its own
Legal execution: stoning as the remedy against sword-proof avengers

title.en: Volund the Smith: The Hamstrung Master and His Wings
title.zh: 鐵匠沃倫德：被斷筋的巧匠與他的羽翼

region.en: The Wolfdales of Sörland (symbolic pin at Småland, Sweden)
region.zh: 斯莫蘭狼谷（象徵性定位於瑞典）

texts.period: Volundarkvida c. 1000-1200; precedent iconography: the Franks Casket (8th c.), Ardre stone (8th c.); principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to

source.work: Volundarkvida; precedent iconography on the Franks Casket and the Ardre VIII stone; English: Bellows 1923

texts.license: Public domain (Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Volund (Wayland), the master smith among the wood-elves, is captured by King Nidadr, hamstrung, and set on an island to forge the king's treasures. His revenge is the corpus's darkest: he kills the king's two sons when they come to spy on the treasure-hoard, fashions drinking-cups of their skulls, gems of their eyes and brooches of their teeth, and gives them to the court; then he betakes the king's daughter, who comes secretly for the broken ring, and flies away on wings he has forged, laughing from the sky while the king's daughter is shamed and the cups testify. The record is the smith-god's dark doctrine: the maker's art as revenge-engineering, and the escape whose vehicle is the craft itself.
summary.zh: 沃倫德（即威蘭）是林中精靈中的宗匠鐵匠，被尼杜德國王擒獲、砍斷腳筋，安置於島上為王鍛造珍寶。他的復仇是語料中最黑暗的篇章：當國王的兩個兒子前來窺探藏金時，他將二人殺害，以其頭蓋骨製成酒杯、以眼珠鑲成寶石、以牙齒做成胸針，獻入宮中；隨後國王之女為尋斷裂的指環暗中前來，亦被他佔有；最後他鍛出羽翼，大笑著自天空飛離——杯中之物自會作證。此記錄是鐵匠之神的黑暗教義：工匠之術即復仇之器，而逃生之翼亦由技藝鍛成。

texts.canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Volundarkvida ('the lay of Volund') is the eddic heroic poem with the oldest iconographic pedigree: the Franks Casket (Northumbrian, 8th c.) and the Ardre VIII stone (Gotland, 8th c.) both carve the story - the hamstrung smith at his forge, the king's sons' skulls, the flight with wings - centuries before the manuscript. The plot: Volund, 'prince of the elves'? - the verse: 'lord of the elf-kind? - smith of the wood, living in the Wolfdales with his brothers, loses his swan-bride (the three valkyrie-wives fly away) and forges rings of red gold, hundreds strung on a bast-rope; one is stolen in the night - and the thief is the king's daughter? - the ring is taken by Nidadr's men, and the king, coveting the smith's art, comes with an army, captures him, and - by his wife's counsel? - by the queen's: 'as he? - the queen's order: 'cut the sinews under his knees, set him on the island Saevarstad, and let him forge for me? - the smith is hamstrung and islanded.

The revenge is plotted in the poem's darkest register. The two boys of the king come to the island to spy on the treasure 'in secret? - and Volund, hiding gems in the trough? - bids them come back silently for gems; then he kills both boys, and the verse's workshop-list: 'he fashioned? - the skulls into drinking-cups (the queen shall drink from her sons' skulls), the eyes into gems (the king shall wear his sons' eyes at his drinking-feast? - set in jewels), the teeth into brooches for the princess - the art's final proof: the court wears and drinks its own children. Then the daughter: she comes secretly for the broken ring, and Volund 'betook her'? - the verse: the smith takes the king's daughter - and then the escape: 'he forged? - the verse: Volund 'rose on the wind'? - the smith has made wings of? - feather-gear (the poem does not specify; the iconography shows him airborne), and flies: 'laughing? - the verse: 'smiling? - Volund 'rose laughing into the air', and Nidadr, sitting maimed-of-sleep? - the king commands his daughter speak, and she tells what the smith has done; and the cups testify: the queen's cup is her sons' skulls.

The record's cultural functions are the smith's-vengeance doctrine and the craft-as-escape doctrine. The smith is the myth-world's industrial class; the poem makes his art the engine of his revenge - the master-craftsman's final products are trophies that force the court to consume its own kin, and his escape-vehicle is made, not stolen: the wings are forged. And the portrait is moral-ambiguous in the corpus's signature mode: Volund's crimes are monstrous and his dignity intact - the poem's last stanza has the king's own son Egil? - Egil, the brother, shoot at the flying smith, who has (per the prose in the Codex Regius) a bladder of blood under each arm, so that Egil's arrows are dyed and the king believes him slain - the trickster's final escape covered by the brother's complicity.

In the atlas, the record anchors the smith-avenger family (the Greek Hephaestus' trap on Ares and Aphrodite, the Chinese Gan-Jiang's son's revenge): each a craftsman's revenge-engineering; the Norse one is distinctive in skull-cups, wing-escape, and the blood-bladder trick.

functions: Smith's-vengeance doctrine: the master-craftsman's products force the court to consume its own kin
Craft-as-escape: the wings are forged, not stolen - the maker's art as exit-vehicle
Moral ambiguity in the corpus's signature mode: monstrous crimes with intact dignity
Oldest iconographic pedigree: 8th-century Northumbrian and Gotlandic carvings

variants.name: Volundarkvida (Poetic Edda)
variants.text_tradition: Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to; prose frame in the Codex Regius
variants.summary: The poem itself with the Codex Regius prose prologue and the Egil-shooting epilogue.

variants.name: Franks Casket; Ardre VIII stone (8th c. iconography)
variants.text_tradition: Northumbrian whale-bone casket; Gotlandic picture stone
variants.summary: The story carved centuries before the manuscript: the forge-scene, the skulls, the winged flight.

variants.name: English Wayland legend
variants.text_tradition: Deor (Old English poem); Middle English ballads
variants.summary: The same smith in English tradition - 'Welond him? - Deor's lament - the pan-Germanic smith-hero.

passages.text: Nidadr hamstrung the smith and set him on the island Saevarstad to forge treasures; the smith's revenge was wrought in the king's own kin: the two boys killed, their skulls fashioned into drinking-cups for the queen, their eyes into gems for the king, their teeth into brooches for the princess.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Volundarkvida st. 20-26 (Bellows 1923); not verbatim.

passages.text: Then the king's daughter came secretly for the broken ring, and the smith betook her; and he forged wings, and rose laughing into the air, while the court learned what the cups held. Egil the brother shot after the flying smith - but under each arm Volund had a bladder of blood, so that the arrows were dyed, and the king believed him slain.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Volundarkvida st. 27-40 with Codex Regius prose (Bellows 1923); not verbatim.
